notes: Model gateway management: structured endpoints, rotation, rate caps and self-metered usage. The console's Model card grows a real endpoint manager instead of the single text line: add, edit and remove failover endpoints (url, model, key-slot chips with presence dots, per-row TEST), a read-only primary row, source chips for env/structured/one-line/invalid configurations, and the old one-line spec kept as a collapsed Advanced disclosure so existing setups keep working untouched. A KEY SLOTS pool editor writes the ten model-key credential slots (a new MODEL_UP_K1..K8 prefix beside the two existing slots) with presence-only display - a value is typed once and never rendered again. Two new knobs ride the same card: candidate rotation (ordered keeps the historical primary-first order byte-for-byte, round_robin walks the chain) and global sliding-window rate caps per endpoint+key (requests and tokens per minute, 0 = off) that skip capped units and still attempt the least-limited one, so a cap can never silently stop a call. Usage & cost gains a self-metered block backed by the product's own log: every chat attempt appends one JSON row (endpoint, model, ok/fail, latency, provider-reported tokens) into a bounded daily file with 90-day retention, aggregated on GET /api/usage/self into 7-day per-endpoint/per-model/day totals, with an optional CNY price table (usage.model_pricing, exact model then default) whose unknown models report cost null instead of a made-up zero. The Overview card shows requests/ok/fail/tokens/cost in the display currency with honest notes for unpriced models and provider silence; the legacy external-metrics panel is untouched. The structured chain parses through the same failover kernel with a deliberately narrower key-slot allowlist (model slots only), refuses both chain representations in one write, and keeps env MYCORE_UPSTREAMS as the top precedence.
